title: Mood and Worry
summary: Low mood, feeling like a burden, worry, and what still brings enjoyment. Includes one safety question. Written for older adults.
clinicianNotes: Contains a safety item that raises a clinician flag. Agree your response protocol before use. Written for adults aged 60 and over. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

guidance.ok: On low mood, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On low mood, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask how long this has lasted and what lifts it, even briefly.
guidance.explore: On low mood, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask how long this has lasted and what lifts it, even briefly.

domains.label: Feeling like a burden
domains.description: Feeling useless or ashamed of needing help.

guidance.ok: On feeling like a burden, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On feeling like a burden, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore how the person's role has changed and how family sees it.
guidance.explore: On feeling like a burden, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore how the person's role has changed and how family sees it.

guidance.ok: On worry and restlessness, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On worry and restlessness, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore the main worries and when they are strongest.
guidance.explore: On worry and restlessness, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore the main worries and when they are strongest.

domains.label: Enjoyment and hope
domains.description: Still enjoying things and feeling hopeful.

guidance.ok: On enjoyment and hope, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On enjoyment and hope, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on small pleasures and people.
guidance.explore: On enjoyment and hope, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on small pleasures and people.

items.text: I feel sad, low or empty for much of the day.
I cry more easily than before.
I feel that nothing will get better.
I feel I am a burden to my family.
I feel ashamed of needing help.
I worry about many things and cannot stop.
I feel restless or on edge.
I feel nervous about being alone.
I still enjoy some things, such as family time, prayer, food or the outdoors.
I laugh or smile at least once a day.
I feel hopeful about the days ahead.
I have had thoughts that life is not worth living, or of harming myself.
